node.label: Steven Hahn
node.date_label: 1983 The Roots of Southern Populism · 2003 A Nation Under Our Feet · 2009 The Political Worlds of Slavery and Freedom
node.description: Steven Hahn reconstructs popular politics in the United States through slavery, emancipation, rural society and the changing nation. The Roots of Southern Populism and A Nation Under Our Feet place farmers and Black political actors within wider transformations. In his discussion of The Political Worlds of Slavery and Freedom, he challenges accounts that make assimilation into citizenship the sole destination of Black politics. He also asks historians to recognize enslaved people’s wartime flight and armed participation as political action. This identity is distinct from Steven C. Hahn, the historian of Creek and Mary Musgrove histories.
node.representative_figures_and_works: The Roots of Southern Populism: Yeoman Farmers and the Transformation of the Georgia Upcountry, 1850–1890 (1983); A Nation Under Our Feet: Black Political Struggles in the Rural South from Slavery to the Great Migration (2003); The Political Worlds of Slavery and Freedom (2009); A Nation Without Borders: The United States and Its World in an Age of Civil Wars, 1830–1910 (2016).

proposed_edges.relationship: Questions a slavery-to-freedom narrative centred only on integration and citizenship
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Nichols’s 2009 feature quotes Hahn challenging a narrative centred on integration and citizenship, and describes aspirations outside that framework. This connection concerns that documented intervention, not all African American historical experience.

proposed_edges.relationship: Interprets enslaved people’s wartime flight and armed participation as political action
proposed_edges.evidence_note: The 2009 feature and direct book quotation describe Hahn’s interpretation of enslaved people’s wartime flight and armed participation as rebellion. The interpretation remains attributed to him; no uncontested ranking of the largest rebellion is asserted.
